name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,572

indicators.note: tossing throws things about, so the letters of the following word land in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: At a Highland games, competitors throw cabers in matching numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossing the caber is a Scottish Highland games event in which a long wooden pole is thrown end over end.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a pair, so braces are twos, things that come in even quantities.

clue.text: British banks maybe make kitchen appliances

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British
banks are an example of institutions that lend money

explanation.surface: British banks diversifying into making household goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests rivers or money; 'maybe' marks it as an example, of lenders.
explanation.definitionFit: Blenders are electric machines used for mixing or liquidising food when cooking.

clue.text: Activity of oddly crude rural git?

definitions.text: Activity of oddly crude rural git?

indicators.note: oddly here means taking the odd-numbered letters, the first, third and fifth, of the following word
activity implies movement and bustle, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of crude
taken as written for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A sneer at what a coarse country bumpkin does for a living.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: farming is what a crude rural git, a rustic oaf, stereotypically does.
explanation.definitionFit: Farming the land is the typical work done by rustic country people, including the crude caricature here.

clue.text: Impressive list of ingredients not about to rise

indicators.note: not tells us that the word for about is to be left out of the longer word
in a down entry, rising means reading the letters from the bottom upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: a recipe lists what goes into a dish
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: An impressive recipe whose ingredients fail to make the cake rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic describes something grand and heroic in scale, so very striking.

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: bum is British slang for the behind or bottom
an ass is a donkey
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A vet hiding in the back part of the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animal doctor' reads as a vet but splits into two pieces, which sit inside a slang word for the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass drum is a large low-pitched percussion piece played in bands and orchestras.

clue.text: Secured in place with unpleasant work to do inside

indicators.note: inside means the job word is placed within the word for with

blocks.note: and joins things, like with
a chore is a tedious task

explanation.surface: Someone stuck indoors with an unpleasant job to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship held fast by its heavy hook to the seabed is fixed, so firmly fastened.

clue.text: New pine trees around London lake

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a different arrangement

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Fresh conifers planted round a lake in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The Serpentine is the curving lake in Hyde Park, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known winding body of water in Hyde Park bears this name, from its snakelike shape.

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters are removed

blocks.note: Gordon Brown was UK Prime Minister 2007-2010

explanation.surface: A former prime minister brawling without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was Britain's Prime Minister from 2007 to 2010; strip off his first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A row is a noisy quarrel or argument, so it means fighting as a noun.

indicators.note: said means spoken, so we want a word that is pronounced like the one for horses

blocks.note: mares are female horses

explanation.surface: Horses claimed to be important officials.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, mares and mayors sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayors are civic leaders of towns and cities, holders of a ceremonial office.

clue.text: Whale food makes a couple of kings sick

blocks.note: K and R are both abbreviations for king (R from Latin rex)
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Something whales eat that disagrees with two monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny shrimplike crustaceans are the main diet of baleen giants like the blue.

blocks.note: first meaning: at a previous time
second meaning, whimsical: more like an earl, a nobleman

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading invents a comparative of earl, as if one could be more earl-like; the question mark flags the invention.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means at a previous time, and jokingly reads as the comparative of a peer's title.

definitions.note: a whimsical phrase, read as the instruction car away

blocks.note: first meaning: a seed used to season bread and cakes
second meaning, split in two: a vehicle being taken off by a truck

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words: a vehicle that is removed is what a tow truck takes.
explanation.definitionFit: Caraway is an aromatic seed used as a spice in rye bread and seed cake.

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out over the air, so we want a word spoken like the one for avoided

blocks.note: to duck something is to dodge it

explanation.surface: A television channel that dodged showing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast channel' looks like television, but channel is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A duct is a tube or conduit through which air or liquid flows, a kind of passage.

clue.text: Article in German on singer in chorus

indicators.note: in places the article within the abbreviation for German

blocks.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
Ger is an abbreviation for German
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A grammar point about a German article sung by a choir member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means the singer comes first, with the article-in-German piece after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in chorus means everyone doing it at once, all together in unison.

indicators.note: in tells us to place the German and helmet pieces inside the word for execution

blocks.note: hanging is execution by the rope
G is an abbreviation for German
lid is slang for a hat or helmet

explanation.surface: A German in a helmet facing the gallows, as a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The German and helmet pieces go inside the execution word, after its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hang gliding is the pastime of flying from hills on a light unpowered kite-like wing.

clue.text: Physicist badly hurt internally very cross

indicators.note: badly suggests something done wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order
internally means only the inner letters of the next word are kept

blocks.note: the letters rearranged
the middle two letters of very
to ford a river is to cross it

explanation.surface: A scientist injured on the inside and extremely angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very cross' reads as furious, but splits: the inside of very, then a verb for crossing water.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Rutherford was the New Zealand-born scientist who discovered the atomic nucleus.

indicators.note: put back means the letters are turned round to read from the end

blocks.note: to drag is to haul
taken as written

explanation.surface: Take a drag on a cigarette, or stub it out again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag' looks like a puff on the cigarette but is a verb for hauling.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll-up is a cigarette made by hand from loose tobacco and a paper.

blocks.note: first meaning: fulfilling, as in matching a demand or standard
second meaning: a gathering of people to discuss things

explanation.walkthrough: 'Satisfying' reads as an adjective praising the conference, but it is a verb form: fulfilling requirements.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a need is to fulfil it, and a gathering for discussion is also called by this noun.

clue.text: Blows up home even less evenly

indicators.note: evenly means taking only the even-numbered letters, the second and fourth, of the word before it

blocks.note: at home means in
flat means level or even
second and fourth letters of less

explanation.surface: Someone at home making things smaller and less level.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate a balloon or tyre is to fill it with air until it swells.

indicators.note: holding means the phrase before it contains the answer within its run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone running happily with the accelerator held open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throttle' looks like the engine control, but it is a verb meaning choke.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle someone is to choke them by the neck, which is to strangle.

clue.text: It's pleasant to listen to European impostor

blocks.note: EU is the European Union
a phony is a fake person

explanation.surface: A European fraud whose voice is nice to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphony is a harmonious, agreeable quality of sound, especially of words.

clue.text: Sir Lancelot possibly to consider returning without giant's head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
returning means going back, so the word for consider is read from right to left
without is used in its old sense of outside, so the reversed word goes around the other piece

blocks.note: to think is to consider
first letter of giant

explanation.surface: Lancelot reconsidering a fight, minus a giant's head he has cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like it means minus, but here it means outside, wrapping around.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot was one of King Arthur's Round Table, so an example of an armoured nobleman of chivalry.

clue.text: Starts to see colourful birds giving dirty looks

indicators.note: starts means the first letter of each of the next words is taken

blocks.note: first letters of see and colourful
owls are birds

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers glaring at brightly coloured birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Scowls are angry, disapproving frowns, the facial expressions known as glares.

indicators.note: start means only the opening letter of the word before it is taken

blocks.note: first letter of standing
a tall story is an unbelievable one

explanation.surface: An incredible hold-up following a standing start in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the unbelievable word behind the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to play for time, to hold things up or stop progress.

indicators.note: can make means the letters are able to be formed into something else

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A talented host who can build motor cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevrolet is an American brand of motor car made by General Motors.

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so we want letters pronounced like the word for goes

blocks.note: goes, in the sense of uses the toilet
A is an abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Reports of someone going off with an American.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'go' is a British euphemism for using the toilet; Pisa is pronounced roughly PEEZ-uh.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisa is an Italian town in Tuscany, famous for its leaning tower.

clue.text: Japanese initially a very abstruse language

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each word in the run is taken

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: Japanese is, at first, a very obscure tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' seems to apply only to Japanese, but it covers all four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Java is a widely used computer programming tongue, as well as an Indonesian island.

blocks.note: W is an abbreviation for with
taken as written
a shout is a yell

explanation.surface: Someone shouting about a called-off event.
explanation.definitionFit: A washout is a match or event abandoned because of rain, so a total failure.

clue.text: Salt water spring perhaps half gone

indicators.note: half gone means the back half of the word is removed

blocks.note: spring is an example of a time of year

explanation.surface: A salty spring that has half dried up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests a water source, but 'perhaps' marks it as an example of a quarter of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean is a large body of saline water, which is what this word names.

indicators.note: poorly means not in good order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A racer ahead of the field but with wheels out of true.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ahead in a race is to have the lead, to be first among competitors.

blocks.note: a slap is a blow
to dash is to run quickly

explanation.surface: A sloppy driver in a hit-and-run accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit-and-run' reads as one crime, but splits into two verbs joined by a plain 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is done hastily and sloppily, without proper attention.

blocks.note: d is an abbreviation for dead
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Luring someone with a dead fish as bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' looks like a noun beside 'dead', but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle an offer is to hold it out as bait, trying to lure someone.
